Plan the subjects and trials of a uSDT study

Source: R/plan.R
usdt_plan.Rd

Finds the design, the number of subjects and of trials per task, that reaches a given power for the tests of the uSDT hypotheses at the lowest cost, the design with the highest power within a budget, or the design that estimates a quantity with a given precision. What is free is given as a range and what is fixed as a single number, so the same function finds the subjects for given trials, the trials for given subjects, or both.

Usage

usdt_plan(
  population,
  hypothesis = c("diff = 0", "rho = 0", "intercept = 0"),
  power = 0.8,
  subjects = c(10, 1000),
  trials,
  cost = NULL,
  budget = NULL,
  precision = NULL,
  combine = c("each", "all"),
  alpha = 0.05,
  signal = 0.5,
  dichotomize = c("none", "influence", "awareness", "both")
)

# S3 method for class 'usdt_plan'
print(x, digits = 3L, ...)

Arguments

population

A usdt_population object from usdt_population(). With several scenarios, one plan for each.

hypothesis

Character vector of hypotheses, written as in usdt_equivalence(): "<quantity> <op> <value>" with the quantity diff, rho, slope or intercept and the operator =, < or >, or "<quantity> in [a, b]" and "<quantity> out [a, b]". The default tests the three point nulls that hsdt() reports.

power

Power to reach (default 0.80).

subjects

Number of subjects: one number fixes it, and a range c(min, max) lets the plan choose it (default c(10, 1000)).

trials

Number of trials per subject in each task, signal and noise trials together: one number fixes it, and a range c(min, max) lets the plan choose it. One value or range for both tasks, which keeps them equal, or one for each as c(awareness = , influence = ) or list(awareness = , influence = ).

cost

Cost of a design, which the plan minimises: a named vector with the cost of each subject (a session, recruitment) and of each awareness and influence trial, in any unit (missing names cost 0), so that a design costs subjects * (subject + awareness * trials_awareness + influence * trials_influence), or a function of subjects, awareness and influence that returns the cost of each design. Needed when more than one of the subjects and the trials is free. With only one free, the plan minimises it.

budget

Largest cost allowed. With a budget, the plan finds the design with the highest power that costs no more, and power is not used.

precision

Named vector of the widths that the confidence intervals of usdt_tests() (level 1 - alpha) should not exceed, by quantity: diff, rho, intercept or slope, e.g. c(intercept = 0.2). With it, the plan finds the cheapest design whose expected interval is that narrow, and hypothesis and power are not used.

combine

"each" plans a design for each hypothesis. "all" plans one design in which every hypothesis rejects H0 in the same study with the given power.

alpha

Significance level of every test, between 0 and 0.5 (default 0.05).

signal

Proportion of signal trials in each task (default 0.5), one value for both tasks or one for each. Each task must have a whole number of signal and of noise trials.

dichotomize

Which tasks are split at the median, as in usdt_data_tasks(): "none", "influence", "awareness", "both", or one logical value for each task. The split fixes the criterion of a task at zero, so its criterion values in population are not used.

x

A usdt_plan object.

digits

Number of decimals printed.

...

Ignored.

Value

An object of class usdt_plan: a list with $design, a data frame with one row per scenario and hypothesis (or quantity, for a precision target) and the columns scenario, hypothesis, subjects, trials_awareness, trials_influence, power (approximate, as in usdt_power()), estimable, width (for a precision target), cost and limit (the free argument whose limit the design reaches, if any). $frontier records the smallest number of subjects that reaches the target with each number of trials, from the closed form. $checked holds the designs the search checked with the draws of the sample mean and covariance, with the number of subjects and cost of each. $settings stores the planning options. It prints one report per design.

How the design is found

The search follows the two approximations of usdt_power(). With each number of trials in the ranges, on a grid of at most 400 values per task, the closed form gives the smallest number of subjects that reaches the power, and with it the cost of each design. The cheapest designs are then checked with the draws of the sample mean and covariance, which see the fits on the boundary, and the number of subjects of each is raised or lowered until those draws reach the power. The search stops when the next design costs more in the closed form than the best design checked so far. A design whose subjects or trials reach the limit of their range, or come within 2% of it, is marked: the range may be too narrow.

The design chosen this way rests on the approximation. Simulate it with usdt_power(plan, method = "simulation") before relying on it, as the approximation is somewhat optimistic for H2 and H3 when the awareness task is unreliable.

Costs

Many designs reach the same power, trading subjects for trials, so the choice among them depends on what each costs. With linear costs and the difference between means (H1), the cheapest number of trials of each task is close to \(\sqrt{(c_s / c_t) (a_t / \tau^2)}\), where \(c_s\) is the cost of a subject, \(c_t\) that of a trial of the task, \(a_t\) the error variance of a single trial (about \(2\pi\) near \(d' = 0\)) and \(\tau^2\) the variance of the difference between the two \(d'\) across subjects, whatever the power.

See also

usdt_power(), usdt_mdes(), usdt_population()

Examples

pop <- usdt_population(dprime    = c(awareness = 0.15, influence = 0.30),
                       sd_dprime = c(awareness = 0.35, influence = 0.30),
                       cor_dprime = 0.3, criterion = 0.1)

# Subjects for given trials
usdt_plan(pop, hypothesis = "diff = 0",
          trials = c(awareness = 64, influence = 200),
          dichotomize = "influence")
#> ── Plan ───────────────────────────────────────────── approximate · power 0.8 ── 
#> 
#>   Subjects     10 to 1000
#>   Trials       Awareness 64 (fixed); Influence 200 (fixed)
#> 
#>   Target   Subjects  Awareness  Influence  Power  Estimable     Cost
#>   Δd' = 0       100         64        200  0.803      1.000      100
#> 
#>   Approximate power. Check the design with usdt_power(plan, method = "simulation").

# Subjects and trials together, with the session time of each in seconds
plan <- usdt_plan(pop, hypothesis = "diff = 0", power = 0.9,
                  subjects = c(20, 300),
                  trials = list(awareness = c(32, 160),
                                influence = c(100, 300)),
                  cost = c(subject = 600, awareness = 4, influence = 1.5),
                  dichotomize = "influence")
plan
#> ── Plan ───────────────────────────────────────────── approximate · power 0.9 ── 
#> 
#>   Subjects     20 to 300
#>   Trials       Awareness 32 to 160; Influence 100 to 300
#>   Cost         600 per subject + 4 per Awareness trial + 1.5 per Influence trial
#> 
#>   Target   Subjects  Awareness  Influence  Power  Estimable     Cost
#>   Δd' = 0       131         80        132  0.902      1.000  146,458
#> 
#>   Approximate power. Check the design with usdt_power(plan, method = "simulation").

# The most powerful design within 30 hours of sessions
usdt_plan(pop, hypothesis = "rho = 0", subjects = c(20, 400),
          trials = list(awareness = c(32, 256), influence = c(100, 800)),
          cost = c(subject = 600, awareness = 4, influence = 1.5),
          budget = 30 * 3600, dichotomize = "influence")
#> ── Plan ───────────────────────────────────────── approximate · budget 108000 ── 
#> 
#>   Subjects     20 to 400
#>   Trials       Awareness 32 to 256; Influence 100 to 800
#>   Cost         600 per subject + 4 per Awareness trial + 1.5 per Influence trial
#> 
#>   Target   Subjects  Awareness  Influence  Power  Estimable     Cost
#>   rho = 0        81        106        206  0.456      1.000  107,973
#> 
#>   Approximate power. Check the design with usdt_power(plan, method = "simulation").

# The intercept within an interval 0.2 wide
usdt_plan(pop, precision = c(intercept = 0.2),
          trials = c(awareness = 64, influence = 200),
          dichotomize = "influence")
#> ── Plan ───────────────────────────────────────────── approximate · precision ── 
#> 
#>   Subjects     10 to 1000
#>   Trials       Awareness 64 (fixed); Influence 200 (fixed)
#> 
#>   Target                  Subjects  Awareness  Influence  Width  Estimable     Cost
#>   intercept width <= 0.2        63         64        200  0.199      0.999       63
#> 
#>   Expected width of the 95% interval of usdt_tests() at the population values.

# \donttest{
# The intercept, whose search checks more designs (several seconds)
usdt_plan(pop, hypothesis = "intercept > 0", power = 0.9,
          subjects = c(20, 300),
          trials = list(awareness = c(32, 160), influence = c(100, 300)),
          cost = c(subject = 600, awareness = 4, influence = 1.5),
          dichotomize = "influence")
#> ── Plan ───────────────────────────────────────────── approximate · power 0.9 ── 
#> 
#>   Subjects     20 to 300
#>   Trials       Awareness 32 to 160; Influence 100 to 300
#>   Cost         600 per subject + 4 per Awareness trial + 1.5 per Influence trial
#> 
#>   Target         Subjects  Awareness  Influence  Power  Estimable     Cost
#>   intercept > 0        25        114        200  0.901      0.994   33,900
#> 
#>   ! intercept > 0: the design is at the limit of `subjects`; a wider range may give a cheaper one.
#>   Approximate power. Check the design with usdt_power(plan, method = "simulation").

# Check the chosen design by simulation
usdt_power(plan, method = "simulation", nsim = 50, seed = 1)
#> ── Power ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────── simulation ── 
#> 
#>   Design       131 subjects; trials per subject: 80 Awareness, 132 Influence (split at the median)
#>   Reliability  Awareness 0.597, Influence 0.650
#> 
#>   Hypothesis  Test              True      SE  Estimable   Power   MC SE
#>   H1 Δd' = 0  Two-sided test   0.150   0.046      1.000   0.920   0.038
#> 
#>   Simulated power: the share of 50 simulated studies, each analysed
#>   with hsdt(), that reject H0 at alpha = 0.05 (Monte Carlo SE at most 0.038).
#>   summary() reports the precision of the estimates.
# }
